verdict.rationale: Proton's own support page on using passkeys in Pass (pass-use-passkeys) describes passkey authentication without passwords, and TOTP generation is separately documented, so passkey support goes beyond TOTP. The quoted text is only a generic definition of passkeys, though, and does not spell out storing passkeys in the vault or signing into websites and native apps. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of passkey storage/creation in vaults, passkey sign-in on websites via the extension, passkey sign-in in native mobile/desktop apps, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an everyday user, the app stores passkeys and signs me into websites and apps with them, not just TOTP codes

citations.quote: Passkeys allow you to authenticate yourself for online accounts without using passwords or passphrases.
Proton Pass can securely generate TOTP codes for websites that you have saved login details for.
